lines.text: When you tap your credit card at a store register, the payment approves in under two seconds.
In those two seconds, your data embarks on a worldwide journey across thousands of miles of fiber optics.
The card's microchip generates a one-time cryptographic token to prevent fraud.
The terminal beams this token to the merchant's bank, which routes it through Visa or Mastercard's global network.
Their supercomputers check for fraud algorithms, then ping your personal bank to verify your funds.
Your bank approves the charge, transmits the confirmation code back, and the register beeps approved.
All of that happened in less time than it took you to blink twice.
